intro.text: The years of your childhood stretch out ahead of you. How you spend them is up to you.

texts.text: You run, climb and wrestle with the other children until your legs stop complaining.
You take up a sport and train until your hands blister.
You take work hauling crates at the market, and your shoulders broaden.
You swim in the river every morning, whatever the weather.
You race the other children up and down the riverbank until you win more often than you lose.
You climb every wall, tree and rooftop in the neighborhood, and fall off most of them at least once.
An old boxer at the local gym takes a liking to you and teaches you to keep your guard up.
You walk everywhere, miles every day, until your legs are as hard as wood.
You practice the sword forms your family keeps from the old days, morning and night.
You train in the temple grounds at dawn, copying the monks' slow, careful exercises.
You play football in the streets until dark, every single day.
You row on the river with a club of older boys and girls who think you're too small, until you prove them wrong.
Your parents drill you on circuit control until you can light a candle without looking at it.
You spend long nights in the family workshop, copying formulas from books older than the house.
You copy strange diagrams from a book nobody else in the family can read. Once, briefly, a candle flame bends toward you.
You practice the only exercise you know: breathing until something warm runs through your arms like a current.
You practice reinforcement on twigs and teacups until they stop shattering in your hands.
Your family makes you memorize the names of every element and spirit until you can recite them in your sleep.
You sneak into the family workshop at night and read the books you aren't allowed to read yet.
A visiting mage gives a lecture to the children of the old families. You understand more of it than you let on.
With no one to teach you, you work through your family's last remaining grimoire, page by stubborn page.
You meditate in the dark until you can feel your circuits, warm threads running under your skin.
You learn that a drawn circle and a spoken word can make a candle flame stand still. You do it a hundred times to be sure.
You collect old books on alchemy and astrology from junk shops, and slowly separate the nonsense from what actually works.
You read everything you can find, from encyclopedias to old newspapers left on park benches.
You spend afternoons at the library until the librarian knows you by name.
You fill notebooks with maps, languages and history, and argue with your teachers about all of it.
You lose whole nights to online encyclopedias, following one link after another.
You pester every adult you know with questions until they start avoiding you at dinner.
You learn a second language from a neighbor, then a third from a book.
You take apart a clock to see how it works, and eventually manage to put it back together.
You study the city's maps until you know every alley and shortcut by heart.
You listen to the radio every evening, news and dramas and lectures alike.
You spend your evenings in front of documentaries and the evening news, taking notes.
You study for school harder than anyone expects, and top your class twice.
You read the history of {place} until you can tell its whole story from the beginning.
You play with every child on your street and soon know every family on it.
You join clubs, go to every party, and learn who knows whom.
You fall in with an older crowd who know the city's back rooms.
You become the one the other children come to when they need a plan, a secret kept, or an argument settled.
You help at every market, wedding and funeral in the neighborhood, and everyone comes to know your face.
You fall in with a group of students who argue about everything late into the night.
You learn to listen more than you talk, and people start telling you things.
You attend the gatherings of the mage families and learn who hates whom.
You spend your evenings in the tango halls, where everyone knows everyone.
You make friends with the musicians who play on street corners, and through them, half the city.
You become a regular in a corner café, where the same faces argue over the same newspapers every afternoon.
You dig through attics, junk shops and flea markets looking for anything old and strange.
You visit antique dealers, estate sales and museum basements, asking careful questions.
You follow up every story of haunted houses and cursed heirlooms you can find.
You befriend an old collector who lets you rummage through his shelves of oddities.
You dig in the riverbank and in old foundations, looking for anything buried long ago.

failTexts.text: You find old buttons, a cracked mirror and a great deal of dust, but nothing with any power in it.
A dealer swears his dagger belonged to a king. It turns out to be a letter opener.
You follow a rumor across the city, only to find the item was sold the week before.
A box of 'ancient relics' turns out to be someone's grandmother's costume jewelry.
You find a genuinely old coin, worth something to a collector, but with no power in it at all.
An antique dealer tells you that you're the third person this year to ask about strange old weapons. That's worrying.

texts.text: You run errands for the neighbors for a few coins at a time.
You help out at a relative's shop after school.
You deliver newspapers before dawn, in every kind of weather.
You take a job in a workshop and learn to work with your hands.
You wait tables in a busy café and save every tip.
You work in an office, filing papers for people who never learn your name.
You help in the family business, whatever it is this year.

quietYear.text: Nothing much happens, which is its own kind of gift.
The seasons turn. You grow a little taller and a little wiser.

warAnnouncement.text: In {year}, you wake with a burning pain in your right hand. Three red marks have appeared on it, interlocking like a crest. You know what they are: Command Seals. The Grail has chosen you. A Holy Grail War is about to begin in {place}.

In {year}, you wake with a burning pain in your right hand. Three red marks have appeared on it, like a tattoo you never got. By that evening, a stranger in black has found you and explained what they are: Command Seals. You have been chosen for a Holy Grail War, and it begins soon, here in {place}.
